findings.headline: Council Tax collected 52.53% at Q2, 0.72% behind target; Business Rates collected 52.90%, 1.57% behind target
findings.detail: The paper says the Council Tax shortfall equals £1.177m in cash terms and that the full-year target of 93.5% is expected to be achieved through additional recovery processes. It attributes the Business Rates shortfall to additional rateable value being added, which pushes the collection rate down as businesses pay by instalments. The executive summary gives the Business Rates shortfall as 1.56%, against 1.57% in the body.
findings.matters: Collection rates behind target at mid-year show the cash timing risk a finance director would track against the full-year assumption, and a lender can compare Slough's collection against the Berkshire councils the paper refers to.
findings.figures: 52.53% Council Tax collected (0.72% behind target, £1.177m); 52.90% Business Rates collected (1.57% behind target, £2.390m); 93.5% full-year Council Tax target

findings.detail: The paper estimates an additional £1.167m of provision would be needed at Q2 to reach the required level. It expects the position to improve through the year due to new recovery processes. It says the Council is reviewing the formula used to calculate the provision and will update Cabinet.
findings.matters: A gap between the provision held and the formula result is a potential charge to revenue, and a change to the provision formula would affect the reported position for any council using the same method.
findings.figures: £10.282m sundry debt balance; £6.771m required provision; £5.604m current provision; £1.167m increase needed
findings.quote: The Council is currently reviewing the formula used to calculate the provision

findings.headline: Contingency of £4.960m has £2.831m allocated and £2.129m unallocated at Q2, with the paper expecting it to be fully spent
findings.detail: The paper lists £0.062m of HR fixed-term staffing and £2.769m for Ofsted inspection costs ring-fenced for the Families First Partnership Programme, transferred to Slough Children First. It says if no further requirement is put forward, the remaining contingency will be set against the wider overspend.
findings.matters: A contingency being forecast as fully committed to cover an overspend shows the in-year headroom is being used up.
findings.figures: £4.960m initial contingency; £2.831m allocated; £2.129m unallocated; £2.769m Ofsted allocation
findings.quote: with £2.831m already having been allocated and the remaining

findings.headline: General Fund reserve is forecast at £22.313m before the 2026/27 overspend, which the paper says would be drawn on if in-year mitigations fall short
findings.detail: The table shows total earmarked reserves of £39.975m after forecast transfers, including an £11m general reserve contribution that will be netted off at outturn. The paper states the Collection Fund surplus of £5.160m will rebuild a Budget Smoothing Reserve and create a new Collection Fund timing reserve of £3.344m.
findings.matters: A finance director would test the reserve position against the size of the in-year overspend, and a lender would see how far the General Fund cushion depends on delivering mitigations.
findings.figures: £22.313m General Fund reserve before 2026/27 overspend; £39.975m total earmarked reserves; £11m general reserve contribution; £5.160m Collection Fund surplus; £3.344m new Collection Fund timing reserve; £13.6m overspend
findings.quote: the General Fund will need to be utilised

findings.headline: DfE to fund the full cost of RAAC removal at Pippins School, with £0.950m added to the 2027/28 capital programme
findings.detail: The paper states the DfE will fund the full cost, which is £0.950m above the £0.5m already in the budget. It estimates the scheme will cost £1m over the current budget, with completion projected for summer 2027 and work due to start on site in February 2027.
findings.matters: A council whose capital cost overrun is met by central government funding is in a different position from one that carries the overrun itself.
findings.figures: £0.950m addition to 2027/28 capital programme; £0.5m existing budget; £1m estimated overspend; summer 2027 completion
findings.quote: the DfE has confirmed they intend to provide the Council with the full cost of removing the RAAC

findings.headline: Service capital forecast is £32.614m at Q2, £7.291m below the £39.905m budget, with 19% spent at 30 September
findings.detail: The paper says actual spend to the end of September was £6.161m, which it describes as reinforcing the possibility of further slippage. The main slipped schemes are the A4 Cycle Lane (£3.324m) and Destination Farnham Road (£1.160m). The paper says the Transformation Programme slippage of £6.500m reflects the Carbon Neutrality programme not starting until 2027/28.
findings.matters: Slippage on this scale, with 19% spent halfway through the year, shows the capital programme is behind plan, and a peer council can compare that against its own delivery profile.
findings.figures: £32.614m forecast; £39.905m budget; £7.291m variance; £6.161m actual (19%); £3.324m A4 Cycle Lane slippage; £6.500m Transformation slippage; £13.791m total GF capital slippage
findings.quote: The forecast for service capital spend at Q2 is £32.614m, a variance of (£7.291m)

findings.headline: Council repaid £30.14m of maturing loans and raised £20m of PWLB EIP loans in 2026/27 to 30 September
findings.detail: Total external debt at 30 September 2026 was £459.69m, of which £338.18m is General Fund and £121.51m is HRA. The paper says a further £15.35m of loans mature between October 2026 and March 2027 and will need refinancing through new PWLB borrowing. It also expects further borrowing in the second half of the year to fund the £42.899m Capitalisation Direction expenditure.
findings.matters: A lender sees the repayment and replacement flow, the refinancing due before March 2027, and the new borrowing needed for the Capitalisation Direction.
findings.figures: £459.69m total external debt; £338.18m General Fund; £121.51m HRA; £30.14m repaid; £20m new PWLB EIP; £15.35m maturing Oct 2026-Mar 2027; £42.899m Capitalisation Direction
findings.quote: Since the start of 2026/27, the Council has repaid £30.14m of maturing

findings.headline: £4.2m of the £27.7m General Fund disposal receipts in the Treasury Management Strategy have been received at Q2
findings.detail: The paper says a further £7m of disposals have exchanged and are awaiting completion. It states that receipts are necessary to finance the Exceptional Financial Support and mitigate debt costs from the Capitalisation Direction. It warns that a shortfall would likely require borrowing, with an estimated £0.055-0.060m annual interest cost per £1m.
findings.matters: Disposal receipts are the funding source for the Capitalisation Direction, so a receipts shortfall changes the council's borrowing requirement, which is central to any lender's view.
findings.figures: £27.7m assumed disposal receipts; £4.2m received; £7m exchanged; £0.055-0.060m annual interest per £1m shortfall; £12m HRA disposal forecast with £1.4m received
findings.quote: disposal receipts of £4.2m have been received and £7m of disposals have exchanged

findings.headline: Cumulative DSG deficit would rise to £55.464m by the end of 2027/28 if the HNSG is one-off, on a forecast £29.9m net movement that year
findings.detail: Table 12 assumes the £13.0m HNSG is one-off and not ongoing, with a 2027/28 unmitigated overspend of £29.9m. The paper states the resulting cumulative deficit would be £55.464m. The figures are shown as a forecast, not a recovery plan.
findings.matters: A deficit that roughly doubles in a year on the paper's own assumptions is the forward exposure a lender and a peer council would use to test the sustainability of the DSG position.
findings.figures: £25.564m brought forward; £29.9m forecast 2027/28 net movement; £55.464m cumulative deficit by end 2027/28; £13.0m HNSG
findings.quote: would therefore rise to £55.5m by the end of 2027/28

findings.headline: DSG in-year overspend forecast at £21.482m, taking the cumulative deficit to £25.564m by March 2027
findings.detail: The paper expects a £13.0m High Needs Stability Grant (HNSG) to replace Safety Valve payments in 2026/27, against a brought-forward deficit of £17.082m. It states the Council intends to disregard variances on individual DSG blocks until the DSG is back in balance, which it describes as the foreseeable future.
findings.matters: A cumulative DSG deficit with no stated recovery date is a long-term liability a lender and a peer council's finance team will both track, and the decision to stop monitoring by block is unusual.
findings.figures: £21.482m 2026/27 in-year overspend; £17.082m brought forward; £13.0m HNSG; £25.564m cumulative deficit by March 2027
findings.quote: In the context of this large and growing deficit, the LA intends to disregard any variances on individual blocks

findings.headline: Adults Services Q2 forecast is £0.827m lower than Q1, as anticipated pressures do not materialise against a £6.642m rebasing
findings.detail: The paper says the 2026/27 budget included £6.642m to rebase commitments, and early-year performance shows some anticipated pressures will not arise. It expects these savings to recur and to be reflected in the forthcoming MTFS. The paper also estimates the Adults in-year mitigation programme will deliver more than £1.5m.
findings.matters: Recurring savings from a demand rebasing are the kind of change a finance director would test against the medium-term plan, and a peer council can compare the assumption that early-year demand is reversing.
findings.figures: £0.827m reduction in Adults forecast; £6.642m rebasing; more than £1.5m mitigation programme
findings.quote: Performance in the first few months indicates that some of the anticipated pressures

findings.headline: £8.307m of the £15.451m 2026/27 savings target has been delivered at Q2, 53.7%
findings.detail: The paper rates £1.340m of the target as green and £3.137m as amber. It rates £2.279m as red and a further £0.388m as unachievable. Appendix 3 gives the delivered share as 53.5%, a small difference from the 53.7% in the text.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another council can compare delivery rates against a £15.451m target at mid-year, and the unachievable element shows how much of the budget has no route to delivery.
findings.figures: £15.451m target; £8.307m delivered (53.7%); £1.340m green; £3.137m amber; £2.279m red; £0.388m unachievable
findings.quote: Of this £8.307m (53.7%) has already been delivered.

findings.headline: Slough Children First forecasts a £15.955m overspend, which the paper says is causing a cash flow issue and prompts a £5m increase to the 2026/27 contract sum
findings.detail: The paper recommends a £5m increase to the Slough Children First contract sum, met from the General Fund pending further in-year savings. It states this will be reconciled at outturn and expected to be funded from a General Fund reserve drawdown at year end. The Treasury Management Strategy provides for a cash flow loan of up to an additional £5m to the company.
findings.matters: A council-owned company with a cash flow loan facility and a year-end reserve call is a direct exposure for the council's finances and for any lender assessing contingent liabilities.
findings.figures: £15.955m forecast overspend; £5m contract sum increase; up to £5m cash flow loan; £41.022m current budget; £56.977m forecast
findings.quote: The forecast overspend in Slough Children First of £15.955m is now causing a cash flow issue within the company.

findings.headline: General Fund forecast overspend at Q2 is £13.604m after £4m of mitigations, an improvement of £6.316m on Q1
findings.detail: The paper reports a headline overspend of £17.604m, offset by £4m of mitigations, giving a forecast net overspend of £13.604m. The Commissioner Review describes this as an improvement of £6.316m compared with Quarter 1. The paper says further in-year savings are still being sought and will be reported at Q3.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare how quickly a £6.3m quarterly movement was achieved against the mitigation plan, and a lender can see that the headline pressure is being reduced but is not yet closed.
findings.figures: £13.604m net overspend; £17.604m headline overspend; £4m mitigations; £6.316m improvement since Q1
findings.quote: In overall terms, this represents an improvement of £6.316m since Q1

findings.headline: The Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026 received Royal Assent on 29 April 2026, and the timescale for its retail licensing scheme is not confirmed.
findings.detail: The paper expects local authorities to license businesses selling tobacco and vaping products, with Trading Standards given penalty and revocation powers. The 2027/28 line of £0.175m is shown as reversing to (£0.175m) in 2028/29.
findings.matters: A new licensing duty with no confirmed start date and cost is one other councils' Trading Standards budgets will also face.
findings.quote: the timescale for introducing the licensing scheme is not confirmed.

findings.headline: The leisure management fee is estimated to rise by £0.300m from 1 June 2027, while a market review of future operating options is underway for the 10-year Everyone Active contract.
findings.detail: The contract began in June 2017 and covers The Centre, Langley Leisure Centre, Slough Ice Arena and Salt Hill Activity Centre.
findings.matters: A contract review with a fee pressure on a 10-year operator agreement is a commitment whose outcome affects the council's recurring costs.
findings.figures: £0.300m management fee pressure from 1 June 2027; 10-year contract from June 2017
findings.quote: A market review is currently underway exploring future operating options.

findings.headline: Property income budgets were never removed after internal recharging stopped, creating a £181k a year pressure, with a further £101k for Observatory House.
findings.detail: Before 2024/25 internal departments used meeting rooms without budgets for them. Internal recharging was stopped, but the income budgets remained.
findings.matters: Income budgets left in place after a recharging change are a control point other councils may check in their own property budgets.
findings.figures: £181k per annum; £101k Observatory House; £0.282m total 2027/28
findings.quote: Internal recharging was stopped, however, the income budgets for property were never removed.

findings.headline: A £0.560m HRA recharge pressure corrects a previous error in the budgeting for Revenues and Welfare Services.
findings.detail: The error was identified during ongoing budget reviews and is based on 2025/26 outturn.
findings.matters: A budgeting error corrected through a growth line shows how prior-year budget reviews are feeding into the next year's pressures.
findings.quote: Correcting a previous error in the budgeting for HRA recharges

findings.headline: Two and a half officers overseeing partnerships and engagement are not funded beyond April 2027, an issue the paper says was identified by a VFM audit and the annual governance statement.
findings.detail: The paper says there will be no resource to maintain strategic oversight of partnership working or basic council-wide consultation and engagement coordination after that date.
findings.matters: A governance gap that was already raised in a VFM audit and the annual governance statement, and is now unfunded, is one a finance director would expect to see addressed in the budget.
findings.figures: £0.184m for 2.6 officers (2027/28)
findings.quote: The 2.6 officers who oversee partnership and consultation and engagement strategic co-ordination are not funded past April 2027

findings.headline: A £2.000m housing benefit subsidy loss pressure relates to 200 additional households requiring accommodation since the MTFS was finalised.
findings.detail: The Housing Temporary Accommodation line also carries a £1.453m staffing pressure to stabilise the core team before Transformation investment. The paper describes the core staffing budget as inadequate for growth in homeless households.
findings.matters: A subsidy loss on additional households arises when accommodation costs exceed what subsidy recovers, so it sits directly on the council's general fund.
findings.figures: £2.000m subsidy loss; £1.453m staffing; £3.453m Housing total 2027/28
findings.quote: Pressure relating to 200 additional households requiring accommodation since the MTFS was finalised.

findings.headline: Temporary accommodation cases rose from 390 to over 1,500, and arrears grew from £1.409m in January 2024 to £12.336m in August 2026.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the arrears increase to the change from charging LHA rate to market rent. It says there is only 0.5 FTE budget to recover TA arrears, and a growth bid for a further 2 FTE is required.
findings.matters: Growth in temporary accommodation cases and arrears, with recovery resourced at 0.5 FTE, shows a demand and income-collection pressure a finance director elsewhere could compare against their own homelessness figures.
findings.figures: TA cases: 390 to over 1,500; arrears £1.409m (January 2024) to £12.336m (August 2026); £0.115m growth for 2 FTE
findings.quote: The number of TA cases has increased from 390 to over 1,500.

findings.headline: Children's Services emerging pressures total £16.799m for 2027/28, the largest share of the paper's £27.428m total.
findings.detail: The directorate total combines the Slough Children First placeholder with the £0.844m SEND staffing line. The paper's summary shows no pressures in the following two years for Children's Services.
findings.matters: Children's Services accounts for over 60% of the total emerging pressures in this paper, so the directorate's movement will largely determine the final 2027/28 gap.
findings.figures: £16.799m Children's Services 2027/28; £27.428m total 2027/28; £27.253m total across three years
findings.quote: Children's Services 16.799 0.000 0.000 16.799

findings.headline: Slough Children First forecasts a £16m overspend in 2026/27, and the paper carries a £15.955m placeholder for 2027/28.
findings.detail: The overspend is linked to placement budgets, associated staffing costs, care leaver costs and a recent OFSTED inspection. KPMG and Mutual Ventures are reviewing demand pressures to provide planning scenarios, and the paper says the placeholder 'will need to be reviewed as the budget process evolves and is likely to increase.'
findings.matters: A £16m forecast overspend at the council's children's company, with a placeholder that the paper expects may rise, is a large and open-ended call on the 2027/28 budget.
findings.figures: £16m forecast overspend in 2026/27; £15.955m placeholder for 2027/28 (table: 15.955, 28/29: 15.955 shown in the table's year columns as 15.955 and 15.955 in the line)
findings.quote: Slough Children First is forecasting an overspend of £16m in 2026/27

findings.headline: Commissioners say the council will face an increasingly challenging position in 2027/28 unless significant improvement is achieved in the final periods of 2026/27
findings.detail: The Commissioner review says the council remains exposed to deficits in 2026/27 and 2027/28, and that the scale of the budget gap is predicted to grow over the strategy period. It also says the ability to drive pace and recalibrate off-track programmes needs strengthening.
findings.matters: A Commissioner statement that the gap is growing, with a stated condition for improvement, is the point a finance director or lender would weigh against the council's delivery record.
findings.quote: Unless a significant improvement is achieved in the final periods of 2026/27, the Council will face an increasingly challenging position in 2027/28 and beyond

findings.headline: The Q2 review finds no material deviation from the GF debt reduction strategy, which targets under £300m by 2035/36
findings.detail: The paper says the debt position is reviewed quarterly and that there has been no material deviation from the reported strategy. The strategy assumed GF debt could be reduced to under £300m by 2035/36, with assumptions on asset disposals, capital investment and MRP.
findings.matters: A lender tracks whether the council is keeping to its published debt reduction path, and this paper states it is on track at Q2.
findings.figures: GF debt under £300m target by 2035/36; £27.7m disposals target; £16.906m of GF-borrowing-funded schemes
findings.quote: there has been no material deviation from the position reported as part of the strategy.

findings.headline: £4.2m of General Fund asset receipts achieved in 2026/27 against a £27.7m target for GF disposals
findings.detail: The paper says further properties are being marketed, and that if sold they would enable the £27.7m GF disposals target to be met. The Treasury Management Strategy assumed £79.4m of GF disposal receipts over 2026/27 to 2028/29.
findings.matters: Asset disposals are a funding source for the debt reduction strategy and EFS, so progress against the target affects the council's borrowing path.
findings.figures: £4.2m GF asset receipts achieved 2026/27; £27.7m target for GF disposals; £79.4m assumed over 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.quote: To date £4.2m of GF asset receipts have been achieved in 2026/27.

findings.headline: Exceptional Financial Support is forecast at £417.4m, of which £336.4m was formally agreed up to 2024/25
findings.detail: The paper's table shows EFS forecast in the MTFS across years. Amounts for 2025/26, 2026/27 and the indicative 2027/28 are agreed in principle or indicative, and will only be formally agreed once accounts are audited and signed off.
findings.matters: The total EFS figure is the scale of central support the council relies on, and whether it is formally agreed is a key point for lenders.
findings.figures: £417.4m total EFS; £336.4m formally agreed up to 2024/25; £15.7m 2025/26; £42.9m 2026/27; £22.4m 2027/28 indicative
findings.quote: The agreed level of EFS as forecast in the MTFS totals £417.4m

findings.headline: The cumulative DSG deficit is forecast at £25.564m by the end of 2026/27, after a £13m High Needs Stability Grant
findings.detail: The paper says the DfE will cover 90% of eligible spend on DSG deficits to the end of 2025/26 through the High Needs Stability Grant, with the remaining 10% addressed through the local recovery and reform plan. Work on a revised plan is ongoing and acceptance is pending.
findings.matters: A finance officer can compare the size of the net DSG deficit and the stability grant route against their own high-needs position.
findings.figures: £25.564m cumulative DSG deficit after deduction; £13m High Needs Stability Grant; 90% stability grant cover; 10% under recovery plan
findings.quote: forecast to increase to a cumulative £25.564m (after deducting the anticipated £13m High Needs Stability Grant)

findings.headline: New 2027/28 budget risks and pressures total £27.428m, largely from increased volumes and demand
findings.detail: The paper says the process identified additional budget risks for 2027/28. It describes them as largely related to increased volumes and demand, and says they are not yet accepted as confirmed pressures. Children's placement pressures are shown at £15.955m as a placeholder.
findings.matters: A large demand-led pressure with no confirmed funding is the pattern that finance directors elsewhere are tracking for their own 2027/28 budgets.
findings.figures: £27.428m new pressures; £15.955m Children's placement pressures (placeholder); £2.000m Temporary Accommodation Housing Benefit subsidy shortfall
findings.quote: Pressures total £27.428m.

findings.headline: A budget gap of £11m for 2027/28 and £18m over the medium term was reported to July Cabinet
findings.detail: The paper refers back to the July Cabinet, which reported the budget gap. It says a material uncertainty remains over the level of savings needed for 2027/28, so a revised gap is not being set out in this report.
findings.matters: The July figures are the baseline that the revised gap will be measured against, and the council is deferring a revised figure because of the Children's pressure uncertainty.
findings.quote: a published budget gap, reported to Cabinet in July, of £11m for 2027/28 and £18m over the Medium-Term.

findings.headline: Usable reserves were 27.13% of net revenue expenditure in 2024/25, fifth lowest of the comparator authorities that have reported
findings.detail: The paper cites the CIPFA financial resilience index. Nearest neighbours held between 11.30% and 84.29% of usable reserves against net revenue expenditure. The council says it will reconsider its reserves strategy in light of pressures identified to date.
findings.matters: The CIPFA comparator range gives finance directors and lenders a benchmark for how far the council's reserves sit from its neighbours.
findings.figures: 27.13% in 2024/25; nearest neighbours 11.30% to 84.29%
findings.quote: fifth lowest out of the comparator authorities that have reported

findings.headline: The General Fund reserve is forecast at £22.313m before the 2026/27 overspend
findings.detail: The paper's reserves table gives a forecast General Fund reserve of £22.313m before the 2026/27 overspend. It states that the General Fund will need to be used if in-year mitigations do not fully manage the forecast £13.6m overspend.
findings.matters: A reader can compare the General Fund balance with the overspend that could draw on it.
findings.figures: £22.313m General Fund reserve before 2026/27 overspend; £13.6m forecast overspend
findings.quote: If the in-year mitigations are not able to fully manage the forecast overspend of £13.6m, the General Fund will need to be utilised.

findings.headline: The 2026/27 forecast overspend is £13.6m, improved from £19.9m at Q1
findings.detail: The paper reports the Q2 Finance Update forecast for 2026/27. It says the overspend could deplete General Fund reserves if in-year mitigations do not fully manage it.
findings.matters: A movement of £6.3m between Q1 and Q2 shows the in-year recovery trajectory, and the reserves exposure if it is not fully closed.
findings.figures: £13.6m forecast 2026/27 overspend; £19.9m at Q1
findings.quote: a £13.6m overspend is forecast for 2026/27, improved from £19.9m at Q1

findings.headline: The remaining £4.4m of operational savings are reported as on track and all fall in 2026/27
findings.detail: The paper says the existing savings programme totals £37.2m, of which £32.8m is transformation. The remaining £4.4m are operational savings, all in 2026/27, and are on track to be delivered.
findings.matters: This is the part of the savings programme the paper describes as on track, which lets a reader separate it from the transformation programme at risk.
findings.figures: £37.2m total existing savings programme; £32.8m transformation; £4.4m operational, on track
findings.quote: The remaining £4.4m are operational savings, all of which in 2026/27, and are on track to be delivered.

findings.headline: £8.307m of the £15.451m 2026/27 savings target is already delivered
findings.detail: The 2026/27 savings target is £15.451m. The RAG table shows £8.307m already delivered, £1.340m on track, £3.137m at some risk, £2.279m at major risk and £0.388m unachievable. The paper says the £0.850m temporary accommodation saving is the largest immediate concern.
findings.matters: A finance officer can see how much of the current-year target is banked and how much is still exposed late in the year.
findings.figures: £15.451m target; £8.307m already delivered; £1.340m on track; £3.137m some risk; £2.279m major risk; £0.388m unachievable; £0.850m temporary accommodation saving
findings.quote: The Council’s savings target for 2026/27 is £15.451m

findings.headline: £26m of the £32.8m transformation savings remain achievable, provided programme management, decision-making and oversight are tightened
findings.detail: The paper says the £26m is achievable if a strengthened PMO works with Inner Circle to deliver stronger programme management, clear decision-making and tighter oversight. The council's contingency is currently fully allocated to the savings that are not deliverable as planned.
findings.matters: It shows the council tying its savings recovery to a specific governance change, and a contingency that has no headroom left.
findings.figures: £26m achievable; £6.6m contingency headroom against non-delivery
findings.quote: £26m of savings remain achievable, provided there is stronger programme management, clear decision-making and tighter oversight

findings.headline: £21.1m across 18 transformation projects is rated Red
findings.detail: Of the £32.8m transformation programme, £21.1m across 18 projects is rated Red, £7.5m across 19 projects is Amber, and £3.4m across six projects is green or completed. A further £0.8m has been removed from the plan.
findings.matters: The share of projects rated Red shows how much of the savings plan depends on recovery work before it can be relied on.
findings.figures: £21.1m across 18 projects Red; £7.5m across 19 projects Amber; £3.4m across six projects green or completed; £0.8m removed from plan; £32.8m total
findings.quote: £21.1m across 18 projects is currently rated Red

findings.headline: About £6m of the £32.8m transformation savings are unlikely to be delivered as originally planned and will need to be replaced
findings.detail: Inner Circle reviewed 50 transformation projects worth £32.8m over three years. The paper says the review concluded that about £6m will need replacing, while £26m remains achievable if programme management is strengthened.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare how much of a transformation programme is being replaced against how much is still expected to deliver.
findings.figures: £6m unlikely to be delivered as planned; £32.8m transformation programme; £26m remains achievable
findings.quote: approximately £6m of savings are unlikely to be delivered as originally planned and will need to be replaced

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1B - 2027/28 and MTFS Indicative Savings Proposals

findings.detail: The Library Service proposal would contribute £100,000 to staffing costs from the Public Health Grant Reserve, and a further proposal would contribute to other directorate budgets subject to PHG board approval. Both are listed in the 2027/28 column.

findings.matters: A new count of learning actions gives a baseline that the six-month update can be measured against.
findings.figures: 288 learning actions identified in 2025/26 (new measure)

findings.detail: The paper says there are no direct ongoing revenue implications from noting the report. It links complaint handling to reduced risk of financial remedies, compensation and avoidable service costs, but gives no amounts for remedies or compensation.
findings.matters: It shows which budget is carrying the cost of the improvement programme, and that the council has not quantified its remedy and compensation exposure.
findings.figures: None given in the paper
findings.quote: it is anticipated that improvement works such as the work being delivered by Red Rock will be funded from the transformation budget approved in February 2026 Full Council

findings.headline: Stage 1 complaints responded to within target rose from 46% to 66% in 2025/26, while total complaints rose 56% to 1,498.
findings.detail: The paper reports Stage 2 responses within target rising from 42% to 50%, and Stage 1 complaints upheld falling from 71% to 52%. It attributes the rise in complaints partly to improved recording and channel accessibility.
findings.matters: Timeliness and uphold figures are the measures Ombudsman codes use, so a peer council or lender can compare them directly with its own position.
findings.figures: Stage 1 within target: 46% to 66% (+20 percentage points); Stage 2 within target: 42% to 50% (+8 percentage points); Stage 1 upheld: 71% to 52% (-19 percentage points); total complaints: 960 to 1,498 (+56%)
findings.quote: Improvements in complaint handling performance despite increased volumes.

findings.headline: Commissioners note the continued increase in complaints and support the actions proposed.
findings.detail: The Commissioner review says volumes and uphold rates suggest recurring service failures and communication problems. It asks for measurable service improvements in high-demand services and evidence that learning from complaints is being applied.
findings.matters: The paper records Commissioner oversight of complaint performance, which a lender or peer finance officer would read as a governance condition on the council.
findings.figures: 1,498 complaints in 2025/26, a 56% increase
findings.quote: Commissioners note the continued increase in complaints and support the actions proposed.

findings.headline: Chief Executive and Monitoring Officer met the Ombudsman over the Council's "failure" to respond in time to investigations and implement recommendations
findings.detail: The paper says the meeting concerned timeliness on Ombudsman investigations and implementation of agreed recommendations, which it says mainly relates to SEND complaints. Meetings are to continue quarterly.
findings.matters: A council meeting its Ombudsman at senior level over unimplemented recommendations is a compliance and remedy-exposure signal that a finance director, or a lender assessing governance, would track.
findings.figures: Ombudsman investigations: 17 in 2024/25 and 17 in 2025/26
findings.quote: The Chief Executive and the Monitoring Officer met the regional officer from the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman to discuss concerns about the Council’s failure to respond in a timely manner to ombudsman investigations and to implement agreed recommendations.

findings.headline: Slough's H1 2026/27 average interest rate on its treasury position was 4.06%, against an average SONIA of 3.73%
findings.detail: The paper says the council's interest rate performance during H1 2026/27 'compares favourably' with average SONIA. Investments were placed with a weighted average rate of 4.06%, against 3.73% average SONIA over the period.
findings.matters: Returns above the overnight benchmark on a sizeable investment book, with security and liquidity prioritised, are a comparison peers will make with their own treasury results.
findings.figures: Actual interest rate performance 4.06%; average SONIA 3.73%; Bank Rate 3.75%
findings.quote: The Council’s actual interest rate performance during the H1 2026/27 was 4.06% which compares favourably with the average SONIA rates as can be seen above.

findings.headline: Slough's net borrowing was £407.6m at 30 September 2026, down from £450.5m at 31 March 2026
findings.detail: The paper reports net borrowing of £407.6m, a fall of £42.9m in the half-year. It attributes part of the movement to short-term investments rising to £40.0m, mainly from £24.5m of NHS grant for the Upton Court development and £4.2m of asset disposals.
findings.matters: A fall in net borrowing driven by grant receipts and disposals, rather than new debt, is a cash position a finance director would compare with their own.
findings.figures: Net borrowing £407.6m at 30.09.26, £450.5m at 31.03.26; short-term investments £40.0m; NHS grant £24.5m; asset disposals £4.2m
findings.quote: On 30 September 2026, the authority had net borrowing of £407.6m arising from its revenue and capital income and expenditure.

findings.headline: Slough's capitalisation direction is £42.9m in both the 2026/27 budget and latest estimate
findings.detail: The capital expenditure table shows a capitalisation direction of £42.9m in both columns, with a related capital financing requirement of £111.7m at 31 March 2027. The paper does not explain the direction in this document.
findings.matters: A capitalisation direction is a borrowing-funded route to cover revenue spend, which lenders and finance officers elsewhere would treat as a distinct and closely watched exposure.
findings.figures: Capitalisation direction £42.9m budget and latest estimate; CFR for capitalisation direction £111.7m at 31.03.2027
findings.quote: Capitalisation Direction 42.9 42.9

findings.headline: Slough expects a DISH lease termination to add £2.5m to its general fund and cashflow in 2026/27
findings.detail: The paper says the lease termination for Development Initiative for Slough Housing Ltd, approved by Cabinet in October 2026, is expected to have a positive impact on the general fund and its cashflow. The paper does not give a basis for the £2.5m figure.
findings.matters: A one-off inflow from unwinding a housing lease is the sort of item a finance director would check against any gap in the MTFS.
findings.figures: £2.5m expected positive impact on GF and cashflow in 2026/27
findings.quote: there will be positive impact to the Council’s GF and its cashflow of £2.5m in 2026/27.

findings.headline: Slough expects Slough Children First to draw up to £5m of its £5.0m working capital facility
findings.detail: The paper says Slough Children First is facing 'significant financial pressure due to increased demand and associated cost' from statutory Children's Social Care Services. The company has provided a cashflow forecast showing a shortfall later in 2026/27. The council will lend only when needed and will seek to fund from internal resources first.
findings.matters: A council lending to its own company to cover a children's services cashflow shortfall is a direct exposure, and peers facing similar demand pressures will see how the loan is structured.
findings.figures: £5.0m working capital facility approved in 2021; up to £5m expected to be drawn; original £5m loan repaid in 2025
findings.quote: This increase in cost is forecast to leave the company with a cashflow shortfall which would make them unable to manage their ongoing financial obligations later in 2026/27.

findings.headline: Slough's latest estimate for year-end borrowing is £497.1m, above its £483.4m operational boundary
findings.detail: The paper says the council operated within its treasury and prudential indicators, but that the operational boundary for borrowing 'could have been set more accurately at the time of TMSS'. It also states that breaching the boundary for cash-flow reasons is not counted as a compliance failure.
findings.matters: A council whose own estimate sits above its operational boundary, and which says the limit was set inaccurately, is a governance point that peers and lenders would check against their own limits.
findings.figures: Borrowing latest estimate £497.1m at 31.03.2027; operational boundary £483.4m; authorised limit £680.8m
findings.quote: while recognising that Operational Boundary for borrowing could have been set more accurately at the time of TMSS.

findings.headline: Slough's general fund financing costs are estimated at £28.5m for 2026/27, against a £22.8m budget
findings.detail: The paper attributes the increase to 'increase in borrowing rates, less income from JEH loan and change of the formula'. The proportion of net revenue stream rises from 11.8% to 14.4%. HRA financing costs move from £3.72m to £4.6m (7.8% to 10.0%).
findings.matters: Financing costs as a share of net revenue are a prudential indicator that lenders and peers compare directly, and the paper links the rise to both rates and the loss of JEH loan income.
findings.figures: GF financing costs £22.8m budget, £28.5m latest estimate; 11.8% budget, 14.4% latest estimate; HRA £3.72m budget, £4.6m latest estimate; 7.8% budget, 10.0% latest estimate
findings.quote: Increase in forecasted expenditure is due to increase in borrowing rates, less income from JEH loan and change of the formula

findings.headline: Slough's latest estimate has £173.7m of internal borrowing at 31 March 2027, against £158.8m in the budget
findings.detail: The council is under-borrowed against its capital financing requirement. The paper says cash supporting reserves, balances and cash flow was used 'as an interim measure in the elevated interest rates environment', and that external borrowing is estimated at £497.1m against a £512.0m budget.
findings.matters: Under-borrowing defers replacement funding but leaves reserves and working capital carrying the gap, which matters to a lender and to other councils using the same approach.
findings.figures: Internal/under borrowing: £158.8m budget, £173.7m latest estimate (31.03.27); external borrowing £512.0m budget, £497.1m latest estimate; CFR £699.3m
findings.quote: was not fully funded with loan debt, as cash supporting the Council’s reserves, balances and cash flow was used as an interim measure in the elevated interest rates environment

findings.headline: Slough repaid a £5.0m LOBO loan to FMS Wertmanagement in H1 2026/27
findings.detail: The paper records one LOBO loan of £5.0m repaid to FMS Wertmanagement, alongside £25.1m of PWLB loans that matured in the period. It says the loans were 'effectively partly refinanced with 10-year EIP loans'. Table 3 shows £20.0m of borrowing raised in the half-year. The paper does not state the coupon of the repaid LOBO or the rate proposed at the call.
findings.matters: A LOBO repayment is a cash and replacement-funding event; a finance director here or at another council would look at the replacement cost and whether the council's rate exposure changed.
findings.figures: £5.0m LOBO repaid (£4.1m GF, £0.9m HRA per Table 3); £25.1m PWLB repaid; £20.0m borrowing raised; 10-year EIP replacement loans
findings.quote: The Council also repaid one of the LOBO loans of £5.0m to FMS Wertmanagement.

findings.headline: Council's investments returned ~4.06% in H1 2026/27, against an average SONIA benchmark of approximately 3.73%
findings.detail: Average investment balances were about £62.4m. The paper says the council prioritised security and liquidity over yield, investing mainly in money market funds and short-term fixed deposits with other local authorities.
findings.matters: A council earning above its benchmark while investing in low-risk instruments gives a peer a comparison point for treasury returns on a similar cash profile.
findings.figures: ~4.06% investment return; ~3.73% average SONIA benchmark; ~£62.4m average investment balance
findings.quote: investments delivered a return of ~4.06%, comparing favourably against the average SONIA benchmark rate of approximately 3.73%

findings.headline: Asset disposals of £27.7m in 2026/27 and £79.4m across 2026/27 to 2028/29 are needed to stay in line with the debt repayment strategy
findings.detail: The paper says the latest Quarter 2 position is in line with the debt repayment strategy for 2026/27, partly because of NHS grant for Upton Court. It also says that an overspend, if not reduced, would adversely affect the debt position.
findings.matters: A council whose debt reduction target depends on specific asset sales within named years gives other councils and lenders a measurable test of whether the plan is delivered.
findings.figures: £27.7m asset disposals required in 2026/27; £79.4m across 2026/27 to 2028/29; £111.0m capital expenditure forecast
findings.quote: the Council needs to dispose of assets in line with the Treasury Management assumption which is £27.7m in 2026/27

findings.headline: Slough Children First forecasts a £15.955m overspend on children's social care costs, with a £5m contract sum variation to be recommended to Cabinet
findings.detail: The paper says a cashflow shortfall would stop SCF meeting its obligations for the rest of 2026/27 unless the council increases the contract sum in-year. It says the company is likely to draw on part of the £5m working capital loan facility, and that the remainder of the pressure is not expected to affect cash in 2026/27.
findings.matters: A council-owned company's overspend that is met through a contract variation and a council loan shows how an arm's-length children's service's pressure reaches the council's own borrowing and cash position.
findings.figures: £15.955m forecast overspend (in line with Quarter 1 position); £5m contract sum variation; £5m working capital loan facility
findings.quote: shows a forecast overspend on children’s social care costs within Slough Children First (SCF) of £15.955m

findings.headline: Operational boundary for external debt is forecast at £525.7m at 31 March 2027, against a £512.0m budgeted boundary
findings.detail: The paper says the forecast breach is an early-warning monitoring measure, not a statutory or legal breach. It attributes the forecast breach largely to expenditure above the General Fund budget, as set out in the Quarter 2 monitoring report.
findings.matters: A forecast breach of a prudential indicator attributed to general fund overspend links the treasury position directly to service spending, which a finance director at another council would want to see reconciled.

findings.quote: Operational boundary for external debt* 512.0 525.7

findings.headline: Council repaid £25.1m of maturing PWLB loans and £5.0m of LOBO loans in H1, refinancing part with £20m of new 10-year EIP PWLB loans
findings.detail: The paper says the repayment and refinancing were supported by a briefing to the Section 151 officer on best value. It does not state the LOBO lender's name, the rate proposed at the call, the coupon on the repaid loan, the original maturity, or the cost of the replacement funding.
findings.matters: A LOBO repaid at par and replaced with PWLB funding is a repayment and replacement event; the council's cash need and the funding cost of the replacement are the figures a lender or peer would compare.
findings.figures: £25.1m maturing PWLB loans repaid; £5.0m LOBO loans repaid; £20m new 10-year EIP PWLB loans
findings.quote: During the period, the Council repaid £25.1m of maturing PWLB loans and £5.0m of LOBO loans and refinanced them partly with £20m of new 10-year EIP PWLB loans.

findings.headline: Total external borrowing fell from £469.8m at the start of 2026/27 to £459.7m at 30 September 2026
findings.detail: The paper attributes the reduction to temporary cash surpluses from NHS grant for the Upton Court development (£24.5m), asset disposal receipts (£4.2m) and other grants not yet spent. Average borrowing cost at 30 September 2026 was 3.67%.
findings.matters: A council holding cash rather than borrowing against its Capital Financing Requirement is a reader's signal of how far the balance sheet is funding capital internally, and how that position may reverse as grant money is spent.

findings.detail: The auditor lists this among the positive developments in the report, alongside the reported delivery of savings and the new shareholder panel.

findings.quote: Reviewing the basis of the asset disposal programme

findings.quote: requiring the Council to implement and embed an improvement and recovery plan to the satisfaction of commissioners

findings.matters: A council under long-running intervention, with a minded to direction requiring quarterly reporting, is a governance position that lenders and peer finance officers would weigh.

findings.headline: The Council's reliance on exceptional financial support and borrowing is named as a risk if the financial sustainability issues are not addressed.

findings.matters: A target date for closing the gap between reserves and budget risk is a clear test that any council relying on reserves or exceptional support can be measured against.

findings.headline: Grant Thornton has issued a new statutory recommendation on corporate grip, dated 29 October 2026, which Full Council must consider within one month.
findings.detail: The statutory recommendation requires elected members and senior officers to take urgent action to ensure effective corporate grip over all Council activities. The Council must prepare a project plan within 3 months setting out how and when it will address key areas of weakness.
findings.matters: A statutory recommendation is the most serious step an external auditor can take, and a finance director at any council would want to see what it requires and the deadlines attached.

findings.headline: Slough's lending and investment over 364 days is currently restricted to non-treasury investments
findings.detail: Section 5.5.6 covers lending and investment for periods over 364 days and is marked as currently restricted to non-treasury investments only. Treasury investments of that length therefore sit outside current practice, and any such investment would fall under the Treasury Management and Capital Strategies.
findings.matters: A council restricting long-term treasury lending to non-treasury investments shows how it is limiting its exposure to counterparty and market risk, which a lender or peer finance officer would want to see when comparing investment policies.
findings.quote: LENDING / INVESTMENT (over 364 days) *currently restricted to Non-Treasury

findings.headline: Slough's short-term borrowing procedure is designed to roll over a short-term loan to keep a £10m liquidity buffer, with the request prepared about 10 working days before maturity
findings.detail: A note to the short-term borrowing procedure says that if a local authority loan is close to maturity and cash flow suggests rolling it over would maintain the £10m liquidity buffer, the treasury team prepares a briefing note and cash flow forecast about 10 working days before maturity. The Section 151 Officer approves contact with brokers about 7 days before maturity. If rollover is not possible, the council may take PWLB loans within its annual refinancing limit.
findings.matters: The fallback from a failed short-term rollover to PWLB borrowing is the mechanism by which a peer council would replace short-term funding, and the £10m buffer sets the liquidity floor a lender would look at.
findings.figures: £10m liquidity buffer; about 10 working days before maturity; about 7 days' notice to brokers
findings.quote: roll the loan over to maintain the £10m liquidity buffer

findings.headline: Slough's treasury practices make new borrowing, other than refinancing or debt replacement, subject to Commissioners' approval during the Government intervention period
findings.detail: The practices state that during the Government intervention period, new borrowing other than refinancing or debt replacement needs the Commissioners' approval. TMP3 adds that borrowing to fund the capital programme or refinance debt is subject to explicit Commissioner approval where it increases the council's overall borrowing position. Section 5.5.2 and 5.5.3 also require all borrowing proposals to be copied to the Commissioners.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender needs to know that new borrowing at Slough currently requires sign-off from Commissioners, which adds an approval step to any funding plan and changes who decides whether the council can borrow.
findings.quote: During the Government intervention period, any new borrowing (other than refinancing or debt replacement) is subject to the Commissioners’ approval.

findings.headline: The auditor's value for money work is complete, and its findings are in the Auditor's Annual Report on the same agenda.
findings.detail: The value for money work for 2025/26 is complete. The findings are set out in the Auditor's Annual Report, which is on the same agenda as this progress report.
findings.matters: The value for money conclusions are the auditor's public statement on how the council uses its resources, which peer councils and lenders read alongside the accounts.
findings.quote: Our work is complete and the findings are set out in our Auditor’s Annual Report

findings.headline: Valuations of land and buildings, council dwellings and investment properties, and the pension fund liability, are still being tested, with no significant matters reported to members.
findings.detail: The auditor is testing the valuation of other land and buildings, council dwellings and investment properties, all rated high estimation uncertainty, and the pension fund liability. Work in each area continues, and the paper reports no significant matters to bring to members at this stage.
findings.matters: Asset valuations and the pension liability are the largest estimates in a council's balance sheet, so finance directors and lenders track whether these estimates have been challenged.
findings.quote: Our work continues in this area

findings.headline: Auditor reports no significant issues to date on management override of control, revenue recognition or expenditure recognition and cut-off, with journals testing 56% complete.
findings.detail: The auditor has selected 147 high-risk journals and has not identified significant issues in its work so far on the three fraud-related significant risks. Detailed testing of these areas is still to be completed.
findings.matters: A council's fraud-risk areas are where lenders and finance directors look for control weaknesses, so an interim report of no significant issues is relevant to their assessment of controls.
findings.figures: 147 high-risk journals selected; journals testing 56% complete.
findings.quote: has not identified any significant issues

findings.headline: 643 of 917 audit samples (70%) have been fully tested and concluded upon, up from 160 of 879 (18%) completed in September 2026.
findings.detail: The number of samples selected rose from 879 to 917 items as breakdowns were received. Initial evidence has been provided for all samples, and 274 (30%) are being reviewed or are subject to follow-up queries.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another council can use the sample progress and the rise in items selected to see how long testing takes when supporting data arrives late.
findings.figures: 917 items selected; 643 items (70%) fully tested; 274 items (30%) under review or follow-up; 879 items selected in September 2026, of which 160 (18%) were completed.
findings.quote: have been fully tested and concluded upon

findings.headline: The Audit Findings Report has moved from the November 2026 committee to January 2027.
findings.detail: The auditor agreed with management to delay the Audit Findings Report, which had been planned for November 2026 and would have been followed by the opinion. Detailed testing will end on 30 November 2026, and the January 2027 report will reflect the position at that point.
findings.matters: The delay pushes the 2025/26 audit timetable back by two months, which affects when peers and lenders can see the auditor's findings on the accounts.
findings.figures: Deliverable planned for November 2026, now January 2027; detailed testing ends 30 November 2026.
findings.quote: we have agreed with management that the AFR will now be presented to the January 2027 AGC.

findings.headline: Auditor stops testing debtor and creditor balances after samples from £6.1 billion and £1.6 billion of transaction listings were found not to be year-end balances.
findings.detail: The auditor selected 30 creditor and 89 debtor items for testing and found that a high proportion were not year-end balances. Testing in these areas has stopped, and focus has moved to 2026/27 planning to address data cleansing for future years.
findings.matters: Transaction listings that do not reconcile to year-end balances show a data problem that other councils with similar ledgers may also face, and it affects how far the council's debtor and creditor figures can be audited.
findings.figures: Debtors in the Financial Statements £58m; creditors £76m; transaction listings supporting them £6.1 billion and £1.6 billion.
findings.quote: The absolute value of the transaction listings supporting these were £6.1 billion and £1.6 billion.

findings.headline: The 2025/26 audit opinion will continue to be disclaimed.
findings.detail: The auditor states that the 2025/26 opinion remains a disclaimer. The paper frames the remaining in-year work as an attempt to rebuild assurance over the longer term.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion on the 2025/26 accounts means the auditor cannot give assurance on them, which lenders and peer finance directors will weigh when assessing the council's financial reporting.
findings.quote: The audit opinion for 2025-26 will continue to be disclaimed.

findings.headline: The Council remains under a statutory direction from MHCLG, with commissioners appointed under a formal direction, and a new direction was issued in November 2024
findings.detail: The paper states the Council has failed to meet its best value duty and is under statutory direction. A new direction issued in November 2024 includes actions linked to risk management, including a review of progress to risk maturity.
findings.matters: Continuing government intervention with commissioners is a material governance fact for any lender or finance director assessing the Council's control environment.
findings.figures: New statutory direction issued November 2024.
findings.quote: the Council being under statutory direction of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) and having appointed commissioners under a formal direction

findings.headline: The external auditors have deemed the 2021 statutory recommendation on a root and branch review not met, the paper reports
findings.detail: The paper says the statutory recommendation issued in July 2021 required reporting on a root and branch review of progress to Full Council, including on risk management. The Council has agreed to report at least six-monthly on its improvement and recovery plan.
findings.matters: An open statutory recommendation from external auditors is a formal audit weakness that a lender or peer finance director would check against the Council's value-for-money conclusion.
findings.figures: Statutory recommendation issued July 2021. Reporting commitment: at least six-monthly.
findings.quote: the auditors have deemed that this recommendation has not been met.

findings.headline: The paper reports no significant treatment-plan milestones missed this quarter, and that the revised-timescale trend seen in Quarter 1 was not evident
findings.detail: The paper says delivery of risk treatment plans remains broadly on track. It also notes some areas still face pressure in maintaining delivery against agreed milestones and timescales.
findings.matters: Whether a council's own action plans are slipping is a direct test of delivery capacity, which a finance director would weigh against planned savings and reforms.
findings.figures: None stated in the paper.
findings.quote: The trend of revised timescales reported in Quarter 1 was not evident this quarter.

findings.headline: The Council’s overall corporate risk position deteriorated this quarter, the first deterioration in 18 months, with five risks worsening, two improving and eight unchanged
findings.detail: The paper reports that the overall risk position has worsened after several quarters of improvement, attributing this to increasing demand pressures and external factors. It also states that the control environment continues to strengthen.
findings.matters: A council's own corporate risk trend is a headline measure of direction of travel that a lender or peer finance director would compare over time.
findings.figures: Fifteen corporate risks in total: five deteriorated, two improved, eight unchanged. Red 9, amber 5, yellow 1.
findings.quote: deterioration in the Council’s overall risk position this quarter, the first in 18 months

findings.headline: CR07, operational resilience, reduced from red to amber, driven by improvement in SR07.05; score 18 matches 18 target
findings.detail: The paper reports one of two corporate risks that improved this quarter. The overall rating moved from red to amber. The current score of 18 matches the target score of 18.
findings.matters: A risk moving out of red is a concrete improvement a finance director could compare against their own resilience and crisis-management controls.
findings.figures: Current risk score 18; target risk score 18. Rating moved from red to amber.
findings.quote: The overall rating reduced from red to amber, driven by improvement in SR07.05.

findings.headline: New corporate risk CR11, Transformation Portfolio delivery, scored 21 against a target of 18, due to scale, pace and interdependency
findings.detail: The paper assesses the overall risk as red because of the scale, pace and interdependency of the Transformation Programme. It notes the Council is delivering savings, service improvement and organisational recovery at the same time.
findings.matters: Savings delivery sitting inside a transformation programme is the kind of dependency a finance director would track when judging whether an MTFS savings line is achievable.
findings.figures: Risk score 21 (current); target risk score 18. Listed in the paper as NEW.
findings.quote: due to the scale, pace and interdependency of the Transformation Programme

findings.headline: CR10, General Fund Asset Disposal Programme risk, has risen from amber to red with a risk score of 21 against a target of 14
findings.detail: The paper attributes the change to market volatility and delays to completion. It says the red position may persist until Q4 2026/27. The risk is one of those flagged for a deteriorating outlook in Quarter 3.
findings.matters: Capital receipts from disposals are a funding source for many councils, so a finance director at another council would want to see how Slough reports delays and market conditions on its programme.
findings.figures: Risk score 21 (current); target risk score 14. The paper gives no £ value for disposal receipts.
findings.quote: this risk has risen from amber to red due to market volatility and delays to completion continue to have an impact

findings.headline: The paper says repeated difficulties in accurately forecasting expenditure have compounded the pressures on the Council’s financial position
findings.detail: The paper links the overspends and the financial sustainability risk to forecasting accuracy, not only to demand. It states that the forecasting difficulties have further weakened the financial position.
findings.matters: A finance director would want to know whether an authority's own forecasting is named as a cause of the overspend, since this affects how far its in-year reporting can be relied on.
findings.figures: None stated in the paper.
findings.quote: Repeated difficulties in accurately forecasting expenditure have compounded these pressures, further weakening the Council’s financial position.

findings.headline: CR09, financial sustainability and balanced MTFS, score rose to 25 against 22 target by March 2027, red with deteriorating outlook
findings.detail: The paper reports that the score for CR09 has increased and the risk remains red. The deterioration is attributed to pressure on the balanced budget and the MTFS. CR09 is one of three risks flagged with a deteriorating outlook for Quarter 3.
findings.matters: The score and target give a lender or peer finance director a numeric measure of how far the Council's own assessment of its medium-term financial position has moved.
findings.figures: Risk score 25 (current); target risk score 22, to be delivered by March 2027. Score movement recorded as an increase, from the prior quarter.
findings.quote: The score has increased and the risk remains red with a score of 25

findings.headline: Children’s Services and SEND overspends are reported as the single biggest threat to the Council’s financial sustainability, with no sum given in the paper
findings.detail: The paper says significant overspends have occurred in Children’s Services and SEND in response to service demand. It describes these as the single biggest threat to financial sustainability. Directorates submitted balanced budgets for the current year.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council facing the same demand-led pressures would want to see how Slough frames the scale of its children's and SEND overspend against a balanced budget.
findings.figures: No £ amount for the overspend is given in this paper. CR01 risk score 24 (target 18); CR03 (SEND) risk score 21 (target 14).
findings.quote: These overspends represent the single biggest threat to the Council’s financial sustainability.

findings.paper_title: IA Progress Report nad Plan Refresh
findings.headline: SEND, rated RED on the corporate risk register (CR03), is being brought into the refreshed audit plan with a wider operational scope than before.
findings.detail: Previous audit coverage of SEND was limited to Ombudsman complaints. The refreshed plan allocates 10 days to a SEND audit, with the intention of widening it to a more operational assurance review.
findings.matters: SEND is a high-cost, high-demand area for councils, and a RED corporate risk rating is one a finance director would expect to see reflected in audit coverage.
findings.figures: 10 days; CR03
findings.quote: SEND – rated as a ‘RED’ corporate risk (CR03)

findings.paper_title: IA Progress Report nad Plan Refresh
findings.headline: A key controls review of Temporary Accommodation is in the refreshed audit plan, building on 2025/26 work including Operation Eden.
findings.detail: The Temporary Accommodation review is allocated 15 days, with a separate 15-day review of Housing Benefit recovery in temporary accommodation. The work builds on what the Service and the Counter-Fraud Team did during 2025/26.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation cost is a budget pressure many councils report against, and the audit's focus on allocation controls and recovery is directly relevant to whether that spend is controlled.
findings.figures: 15 days (Allocation Controls); 15 days (Housing Benefit Recovery in TA)
findings.quote: a key controls review, building on the work undertaken by the Service and the Counter-Fraud Team during 2025/26

findings.paper_title: IA Progress Report nad Plan Refresh
findings.headline: Internal Audit expects to deliver 30 audits in 2026/27, the same number as 2025/26, with fewer resources.
findings.detail: At mid-year 11 audits are complete (6 final and 5 at draft), representing 31% of the Plan, with a further 20 audits in progress. The team is working with Directors and Heads of Service to close the draft reports.
findings.matters: A council delivering the same audit volume with fewer resources is showing the capacity trade-off a finance director at any authority with a reduced internal audit team would be weighing.
findings.figures: 30 audits; 11 completed audits (6 final plus 5 draft); 31% of the Plan; 20 audits in progress
findings.quote: on course to deliver a similar sized audit programme, 30 audits, as that achieved in 2025/26 but with fewer resources

findings.paper_title: IA Progress Report nad Plan Refresh
findings.headline: Recruitment of a permanent Head of Internal Audit was unsuccessful, and interim arrangements will continue while a second options appraisal is undertaken.
findings.detail: A revised job description was advertised and a formal interview process held before the recruitment failed. A second options appraisal will determine a more permanent operating model, with progress reported periodically to the Committee.
findings.matters: Failure to recruit a permanent head of audit is a leadership-capacity issue that other councils' finance and governance teams may recognise in their own audit functions.
findings.quote: Unfortunately, that process proved unsuccessful, and it was agreed that the interim arrangements would continue.

findings.paper_title: IA Progress Report nad Plan Refresh
findings.headline: An Interim Auditor was added for the first half of 2026/27 and will continue to year-end at c. £70k, funded by a drawdown from reserves.
findings.detail: The arrangement was reviewed through Expenditure Control procedures. The revised audit plan depends on the interim auditor's days being included.
findings.matters: A call on reserves to fund internal audit capacity is a spending decision a finance director would track against the reserves position.
findings.quote: The cost is c. £70k and is being funded by a drawdown from reserves.

findings.paper_title: IA Progress Report nad Plan Refresh
findings.headline: St Mary's C of E Primary School received a Partial Assurance audit opinion while forecasting a surplus of over £500,000.
findings.detail: The audit found weaknesses in governance and procurement, including no dedicated finance committee, a financial policy not reviewed since 2021/22, inappropriate procurement card controls, and public funds used for staff hospitality and incentive schemes. The school has begun corrective actions, including establishing a Business Committee and discontinuing incentive schemes.
findings.matters: Procurement card misuse and spending on staff hospitality from school budgets are control failures a finance officer at any council with maintained schools would check their own schools for.
findings.figures: Partial Assurance; forecast surplus of over £500,000
findings.quote: received a Partial Assurance audit opinion

findings.paper_title: IA Progress Report nad Plan Refresh
findings.headline: The Emergency Planning & Business Continuity audit concluded with a Minimal Assurance opinion.
findings.detail: The audit identified weaknesses including the absence of a fully operational Emergency Response Plan, limited business continuity planning and a lack of regular testing. Management has begun implementing a revised Emergency Response Plan, a Corporate Resilience Group and a training programme, and the report notes the audit took place both before and just after a new Emergency Planning officer was in post.
findings.matters: A minimal opinion on business continuity is a governance and resilience gap that a finance director would want to see addressed, since it bears on how the council responds to disruption to its services and finances.
findings.figures: Minimal Assurance opinion; 21 recommendations issued across 2026/27 audits to date
findings.quote: concluded with a Minimal Assurance opinion, identifying significant weaknesses in governance, planning and resilience

findings.paper_title: IA Progress Report nad Plan Refresh
findings.headline: The Adults' Finance Resilience audit gave a Substantial Assurance opinion, with all nine key controls tested operating effectively and no recommendations.
findings.detail: The review covered governance, budget monitoring, demand-led cost pressures, savings delivery and risk management in Adult Social Care. The audit found no control weaknesses, findings or recommendations.
findings.matters: It is a finance-resilience audit of adult social care, a demand-led budget area, that a finance director can compare against their own savings-tracking and market-sustainability controls.
findings.figures: nine key controls tested; Substantial Assurance; no recommendations
findings.quote: all nine key controls tested were operating effectively

findings.paper_title: Update on independent review into housing processes report

findings.detail: The paper says discovery work identified a full programme of change across housing IT systems, including process and training. The plan sets out priorities for the allocations module and temporary accommodation in phase 1.
findings.matters: A dated delivery plan for housing systems sets a timetable a finance director can track against any investment the council must make.
findings.figures: Plan period: now to March 2028
findings.quote: This has been developed into a plan of improvement from now to March 2028.

findings.paper_title: Update on independent review into housing processes report
findings.headline: Temporary accommodation provider rates are governed by a formal rate card, with approval levels for any variance from rates.
findings.detail: The paper says weaknesses were found in pricing and rates, approvals, contract monitoring and review for temporary accommodation providers. Controls have been put in place in response, including the rate card and tiered approvals for variances.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation is a major cost for many councils, and a rate card with tiered approvals is a specific cost control that peers and finance officers could compare against their own arrangements.
findings.figures: None given in the paper
findings.quote: including a formal rate card for provision and approval processes at different levels for any variance from rates.

findings.paper_title: Update on independent review into housing processes report

findings.matters: A gap of several months between audit completion and formal reporting to the audit committee is a governance point that other councils' audit committees would also look at.

findings.quote: The fraud matter was presented to Audit Committee in September 2025, however the audit was not completed until January 2026 and has not been formally reported to the Committee.

findings.paper_title: Update on independent review into housing processes report
findings.headline: Two high-risk recommendations on the permanent staffing structure and recruitment are showing red for progress.
findings.detail: The two recommendations relate to agreeing a permanent staffing structure and recruiting to it, in both temporary accommodation and allocations. The paper describes this as a long-term action.
findings.matters: Red high-risk recommendations on staffing show that the council's remediation of the audit findings is behind schedule.
findings.figures: 2 recommendations recorded as high risk, showing red
findings.quote: Two recommendations that were recorded as high risk are currently showing as red in terms of progress.

findings.paper_title: Update on independent review into housing processes report
findings.headline: A business case for the housing service has been drafted and will be costed and challenged through council governance in the coming months.

findings.matters: A restructure with a costed business case will change the service's permanent staffing mix and cost base, which affects how the council plans its housing budget.
findings.figures: None given in the paper
findings.quote: A business case for the service has been drafted and will be costed and challenged through council governance in the coming months.

findings.paper_title: Update on independent review into housing processes report
findings.headline: Staffing and non-staffing resourcing implications are being considered in the 2027/28 budget setting process.
findings.detail: The paper says staffing resourcing implications are being considered as part of budget setting. Any non-staffing resourcing or invest-to-save options will also need to go through the same process.
findings.matters: The cost of rebuilding the housing service has not yet been set in the budget, so the 2027/28 position depends on decisions still to come.
findings.figures: None given in the paper
findings.quote: are being considered as part of the budget setting process for 2027/28

findings.paper_title: Update on independent review into housing processes report
findings.headline: The housing directorate reports 80% of its staff as interim.
findings.detail: The paper says overall staffing levels are very low and that team funding relies heavily on temporary funding. It says the interim share creates vulnerability around staffing levels, training and policy compliance.
findings.matters: A high interim share and temporary funding base are recurring cost and continuity risks that a finance director would need to price into the budget and into any replacement funding.
findings.figures: 80% of directorate staff are interim ("up 80%" as written in the paper)
findings.quote: Across the directorate up 80% of the staff are interim.

findings.headline: The paper lists commercial investments and debt exposure as a forward focus for assurance in 2026/27
findings.detail: Under financial sustainability in the forward look, the paper lists ensuring the adequacy of reserves and medium-term financial planning, strengthening scrutiny of savings programmes, and assurance over commercial investments and debt exposure as key issues.
findings.matters: Commercial investment and debt exposure are the main areas where a lender assesses a council's borrowing risk, and the paper names them as an assurance gap.
findings.quote: Assurance over commercial investments and debt exposure

findings.detail: The paper says James Elliman Homes has been unable to file audited accounts within the statutory period for several years, and that accounting errors are still being identified for both JEH and GRE5. It also says the Council approved an exit strategy for GRE5 and commissioned an options appraisal for JEH.
findings.matters: Late filing and accounting errors in council-owned companies are a consolidation risk for group accounts, and a lender will want to see how the council is dealing with its controlled entities.
findings.quote: JEH has been unable to file audited accounts within the statutory time period for several years

findings.headline: The Council has made significant progress closing historic accounts and is on track to publish draft accounts within the statutory timetable
findings.detail: The paper says the Council has made significant progress in closing off historic accounts, and is now on track to publish draft accounts in accordance with the statutory timetable. Because earlier accounts were disclaimed, it says the 2025/26 audit will be the first full audit, so the quality of the process cannot yet be assessed.
findings.matters: Publication against the statutory timetable after disclaimed accounts is a measure a finance director and lender can check directly against the audited outcome.
findings.quote: The Council has made significant progress in closing off historic accounts and is now on track to publish its draft accounts in accordance with the statutory timetable.

findings.headline: Forvis Mazars reviewed temporary and permanent accommodation placements after allegations of housing fraud, and its January 2026 report made 22 recommendations
findings.detail: Forvis Mazars was commissioned after allegations of housing fraud and concerns about internal controls over placement decisions. The report, finalised on 9 January 2026, recommended 6 changes to process mapping, 9 for temporary accommodation placements and 7 for permanent allocation placements, and identified fraud and financial risks from manual data entry.
findings.matters: A review that identifies duplicate or erroneous payment risk in temporary accommodation spending is directly relevant to any council carrying similar pressures, and to lenders assessing control weaknesses.
