findings.quote: Forvis Mazars LLP were commissioned to undertake an independent review of temporary and permanent accommodation placements following allegations of housing fraud

findings.headline: The paper identifies insufficient budget for SEND and temporary accommodation demand, with no clear plans yet to mitigate these pressures
findings.detail: The paper says budgets have been aligned to service priorities and baselines made more accurate, but says there is concern around insufficient budget to manage demand for SEND and temporary accommodation. It says there is a lack of clear plans to mitigate these pressures.
findings.matters: SEND and temporary accommodation are two of the fastest-growing cost pressures for councils, and a finance director at another council will recognise this as a live budget risk.
findings.quote: there is concern around insufficient budget to manage demand for SEND and temporary accommodation with a lack of clear plans to mitigate these pressures

findings.headline: The MHCLG commissioners' sixth report, published in July 2025, says targeted net income from asset disposals is not delivering the expected value
findings.detail: The sixth commissioners' report describes the finances as a significant concern, with targeted net income from asset disposals not delivering the expected value. It also says the new target operating model is not yet combined with a strategic transformation plan.
findings.matters: Capital receipts from disposals are a common funding source for transformation and debt reduction, and shortfalls affect how councils plan to fund reserves and capital spending.
findings.quote: targeted net income from asset disposals not delivering the expected value

findings.headline: The permanent monitoring officer left the Council in March 2026, after five different post holders since 2021
findings.detail: The paper says the permanent monitoring officer left in March 2026. It also says the shared legal service with the London Borough of Harrow has provided deputies, and that a senior lawyer from that practice has now been appointed Monitoring Officer.
findings.matters: The monitoring officer holds statutory responsibility for lawfulness and reporting on financial impropriety, so a turnover of this kind is relevant to governance assurance at any council.
findings.figures: five different post holders since 2021; permanent monitoring officer left March 2026
findings.quote: The permanent monitoring officer left the Council in March 2026.

findings.headline: The Council has had six s.151 officers since 2021, and has appointed an interim post holder since September 2025
findings.detail: The paper reports high turnover in the s.151 officer post and says the Council has appointed a highly experienced interim post holder since September 2025. It also notes that the Council has self-assessed against the CIPFA statement on the CFO role, with substantial assurance on leadership influence.
findings.matters: Continuity in the s.151 role affects the reliability of financial reporting and budget control, and a finance director at another council or a lender will want to know who holds it.
findings.figures: six post holders since 2021; interim post holder since September 2025
findings.quote: There has been high turnover in s.151 officers, with six post holders since 2021.

findings.headline: The 2025/26 annual internal audit opinion is 'limited assurance', an improvement from 'no assurance' in 2024/25
findings.detail: The paper says interim CIPFA resource led to an annual opinion of limited assurance for 2025/26, reflecting a full audit programme that gave sufficient coverage. The team completed 30 audits and issued 174 recommendations, with cross-cutting themes of records management, accountability, process and collaboration.
findings.matters: A change in the internal audit opinion is a clear, comparable measure of control environment movement, and the recommendation count shows the scale of remediation work still open.
findings.figures: limited assurance (2025/26); no assurance (2024/25); 30 audits; 174 recommendations
findings.quote: This is an improvement from the issue of no assurance in 2024/25

findings.headline: The Council's self-assessed compliance with the CIPFA Financial Management Code rose to 50% of criteria as at March 2026, from 38% at March 2025

findings.matters: Movement against the FM Code is a measurable indicator that a finance director at another council, or a lender, can compare against their own self-assessments.

findings.quote: As at March 2026 the Council has self-assessed itself as being compliant with 50% of the criteria, with the remaining 50% having reasonable, partial or minimal assurance.

findings.headline: The commissioners' seventh report, published in March 2026, cites a significant in-year financial gap and limited progress on mitigating savings
findings.detail: The MHCLG commissioners' seventh report says previous progress has plateaued, with serious financial challenges emerging. It also identifies slow progress on a credible transformation plan and the need to move from budget growth to efficiencies.
findings.matters: A government commissioner reporting an in-year gap and weak savings delivery is a direct signal about in-year budget risk and the likelihood of further government intervention.
findings.quote: Significant in-year financial gap and limited progress on mitigating savings.

findings.headline: The paper says 2024/25 'resulted in a significant overspend', tied to poor identification and delivery of savings proposals and mitigation of pressures

findings.matters: Savings identification and delivery failures are a common cause of overspends across councils, and the paper gives a specific account of where this council's failed.
findings.quote: the last financial year demonstrated the issue with poor identification and delivery of savings proposals and mitigation of pressures, resulting in a significant overspend

findings.headline: The Council remains reliant on exceptional financial support under a capitalisation direction, and its s.151 officer's s.25 report says it is not financially sustainable without that support

findings.matters: Capitalisation directions are a form of government-approved funding for revenue pressures, and a finance director or lender will want to know that the council's budget depends on this support.
findings.quote: In addition the Council remains reliant on exceptional financial support in accordance with a capitalisation direction

findings.headline: Grant Thornton's interim value for money report for 2024/25 rates financial sustainability, governance and improving economy, efficiency and effectiveness red, as in 2023/24 and previous recent years
findings.detail: The paper reports that financial sustainability has three significant weaknesses, carried over from prior years and still of critical importance in 2024/25, covering MTFS financial viability, levels of reserves and development of financial plans. One statutory and three key recommendations were retained, and one new key recommendation was added on governance.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, can see the external auditor's current view of this council's financial sustainability, which underpins its borrowing capacity and reserves position.
findings.figures: three significant weaknesses (financial sustainability); one statutory and three key recommendations retained; one new key recommendation added (governance)
findings.quote: three significant weaknesses were identified in prior years and remain of critical importance in 2024/25 relating to MTFS financial viability, levels of reserves and development of financial plans

findings.headline: Auditor expects a disclaimed opinion on the 2025/26 financial statements
findings.detail: The council provided draft accounts by the national deadline of 30 June 2026. The auditor expects to issue a disclaimed opinion, with the Audit Findings Report to be presented on 21 January 2027. The backstop date for the 2025/26 audit is 31 January 2027.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means the auditor could not form an opinion on the accounts, which lenders and peer councils read as a limit on assurance over the council's financial position.
findings.figures: Draft accounts provided by 30 June 2026; audit backstop date 31 January 2027
findings.quote: The Council provided draft accounts in line with the national deadline of 30 June 2026.

findings.headline: 64% of planned 2025/26 operational savings delivered, with a savings tracker agreed for 2026/27
findings.detail: The paper lists this among positive developments in 2025/26. It is one of the few delivery measures for savings in the document.
findings.matters: A delivery rate against planned operational savings is a comparable measure that finance directors use to judge budget credibility.
findings.figures: 64% of planned operational savings for 2025/26 delivered
findings.quote: 64% of planned operational savings for 2025/26 delivered; and savings tracker agreed for use in 2026/27.

findings.headline: Council plans £15.6m revenue investment over three years to deliver £25m transformation savings
findings.detail: The auditor says the transformation programme was not scheduled to start during 2025/26 and that the council plans to procure a lead transformation delivery partner. The paper also notes an estimated £20 million of one-off General Fund capital investment in transformation over the same period.
findings.matters: The payback ratio and timing of a transformation programme are the key test for lenders assessing whether a council can exit EFS dependency.
findings.figures: £15.6 million General Fund revenue investment over three years; £25 million transformation savings; £20 million one-off capital investment
findings.quote: The Council is planning to invest £15.6 million of General Fund revenue budget over the next three years, to deliver transformation savings of £25 million.

findings.headline: Children's services overspend forecast at £16m in 2026/27 on rising placement numbers and unit costs
findings.detail: The paper reports that Slough Children's First Ltd is expected to overspend in 2026/27 based on Quarter One data, driven by growth in placement numbers and in average unit costs.
findings.matters: Placement volume and unit cost growth at this scale are a demand pressure other councils with children's trusts or similar arrangements would track.
findings.figures: £16 million forecast overspend for Slough Children's First Ltd in 2026/27; 26% growth in number of children in placements; 40% growth in average unit costs
findings.quote: Slough Children’s First Ltd is expected to overspend by £16 million in 2026/27, driven by a 26% growth in the number of children in placements and a 40% growth in the average unit costs.

findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit forecast at £33.4m by end 2026/27, with High Needs Stability Grant application deferred
findings.detail: The auditor notes the council has participated in the DfE Safety Valve programme since 2022 yet forecasts a cumulative DSG deficit. On 5 October 2026 the High Needs Stability Grant application was deferred pending a revised SEND Reform Plan.
findings.matters: A cumulative DSG deficit that is not reducing under a Safety Valve arrangement is a funding risk for councils with similar SEND pressures and a potential call on reserves.
findings.figures: £33.4 million cumulative DSG deficit forecast by end of 2026/27
findings.quote: forecasts indicated a cumulative Dedicated Schools Grant deficit of £33.4 million by the end of 2026/27.

findings.headline: MTFS carries £5m risk for underwriting losses in group companies
findings.detail: The auditor notes that the Medium-Term Financial Strategy includes this risk allowance, with ongoing review of business plans and exit strategies. The key recommendation requires plans for winding up subsidiaries that are not delivering value to be agreed by the end of 2026/27.
findings.matters: Subsidiary losses that fall to the council add to EFS dependency, and a wind-up timetable is a concrete test for other councils with companies of their own.
findings.figures: £5 million risk allowance for group company losses
findings.quote: The Medium-Term Financial Strategy for 2026/27 to 2028/29 factors in risk of £5 million for the potential need to underwrite losses in group companies

findings.headline: Council's self-assessment against CIPFA's Financial Management Code finds 50% substantially compliant and 35% reasonably compliant
findings.detail: The March 2026 self-assessment is described as providing a strong foundation for continued improvement, with a comprehensive action plan to reach full compliance alongside the Financial Improvement Programme during 2026/27. A baseline CIPFA assessment was conducted in May 2025.
findings.matters: Finance directors elsewhere use the FM Code self-assessment as a benchmark, and a published compliance split gives a comparable measure of financial management maturity.
findings.figures: 50% of the Code substantially compliant; 35% reasonably compliant
findings.quote: The assessment identified a strong foundation, with 50% of the Code assessed as substantially compliant and 35% as reasonably compliant, providing a platform for continued improvement.

findings.headline: Head of Internal Audit post vacant in 2025/26 and 19 open corporate fraud investigations
findings.detail: The paper says the Head of Internal Audit's opinion gave limited assurance over risk management, governance and internal control, an improvement on no assurance in 2024/25. None of the reasonable or substantial assurance opinions related to financial systems. The auditor has made a statutory recommendation requiring the internal audit team to be resourced within six months.
findings.matters: Internal audit and fraud capacity underpin the assurance a lender or peer council relies on, and a vacant head of internal audit with open fraud cases is a governance point in its own right.
findings.figures: 19 open investigation cases; Limited Assurance opinion in 2025/26, compared with no assurance in 2024/25
findings.quote: The corporate anti-fraud team have 19 open investigation cases.

findings.headline: £11.4m of demand growth risk remains in the 2026/27 to 2028/29 budget and medium-term plan
findings.detail: A bridge model exercise in August 2025 looked at reducing demand and unit costs to statistical neighbour levels. The auditor reports the benefits of this approach but says £11.4 million of demand growth risk remains unaddressed in the medium-term plan.
findings.matters: A quantified demand risk in a medium-term plan, with an explicit comparison to statistical neighbours, is a benchmark other councils can use to test their own assumptions.
findings.figures: £11.4 million demand growth risk; £11.7 million potential increase in demand for statutory services in the MTFS risk allowance
findings.quote: there remains £11.4 million of demand growth risk in the budget and medium-term financial plan for 2026/27 to 2028/29

findings.headline: General Fund capital spend in 2025/26 was £33.4m against a £43.1m budget
findings.detail: The paper attributes most of the underspend to regeneration, housing and environment (£5.9 million) and transformation (£2.4 million). Most of the delayed spend is funded from grants and s106 receipts and will be carried forward, but transformation spend will not be carried forward. The HRA capital programme underspent by £6.1 million.
findings.matters: Delivery of capital programmes against budget is a signal of project management capacity, and the carry-forward treatment affects future funding needs.
findings.figures: £33.4 million GF capital spend; £43.1 million GF budget; £5.9 million regeneration, housing and environment underspend; £2.4 million transformation underspend; £6.1 million HRA underspend
findings.quote: The Council spent £33.4 million on the General Fund capital programme in 2025/26, against a budget of £43.1 million.

findings.headline: Net external borrowing of £442.8m at March 2026 forecast to rise to £523.7m by March 2028
findings.detail: The paper reports gross interest of £20.7 million and MRP of £19.7 million in 2025/26. It forecasts net borrowing to fall to £482 million by 31 March 2030, and notes that £13.5 million of the EFS requested for 2026/27 covers financing costs of EFS borrowing.
findings.matters: The forecast rise in net borrowing and the financing cost of EFS borrowing are central to lenders' assessment of the council's debt trajectory.
findings.figures: £442.8 million net external borrowing at end 2025/26; £523.7 million forecast by end 2027/28; £482 million forecast by 31 March 2030; £20.7 million gross interest; £19.7 million MRP; £13.5 million EFS financing cost
findings.quote: The Council had net external borrowing at the end of 2025/26 of £442.8 million; and this is forecast to rise to £523.7 million by the end of 2027/28.

findings.headline: Net asset disposal receipts in 2025/26 were £2.3m against a planned £8m
findings.detail: The auditor says the shortfall indicates that planned future net receipts may not be achievable. The revised disposals profile assumes £79.4 million of disposals across 2026/27 to 2028/29, and the auditor raises a statutory recommendation to review the programme.
findings.matters: The debt reduction strategy depends on asset sales, so a receipts shortfall against plan is a direct risk to borrowing trajectory for lenders and for councils with similar disposal plans.
findings.figures: £2.3 million net disposal receipts in 2025/26; £8 million planned; £21.7 million assumed across 2026/27 and 2027/28; £79.4 million assumed over 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.quote: in 2025/26 the level of net disposals receipts were lower than planned at £2.3 million compared to a plan of £8 million

findings.headline: General and Non-Restricted Reserves forecast at £33.6m by March 2029 against a £37.1m minimum
findings.detail: The March 2026 Reserves Strategy forecasts reserves below the minimum required by 31 March 2029, even after planned replenishments of about £16 million. The paper notes a £5 million Redundancy Reserve could be repositioned to cover the shortfall.
findings.matters: A forecast shortfall against the minimum reserve level, with the gap dependent on EFS and reserve repositioning, is central to the council's medium-term resilience.
findings.figures: £33.6 million forecast reserves at 31 March 2029; £37.1 million minimum required; about £16 million planned replenishment; £5 million Redundancy Reserve
findings.quote: the Council forecasted that it was on track to hold actual General and Non-Restricted Reserves by 31 March 2029 of £33.6 million (therefore lower than required).

findings.headline: Quarter One data for 2026/27 shows a forecast overspend of £19 million
findings.detail: The auditor notes that Quarter One 2026/27 data indicates a forecast overspend, which may mean more EFS is required. This follows the 2025/26 overspend and the EFS requirement already reported.
findings.matters: A forecast overspend in the first quarter of the year, after a year of containment, indicates whether the 2026/27 budget is holding.
findings.figures: £19 million forecast overspend in 2026/27
findings.quote: Quarter One data for 2026/27 indicates that the Council is forecasting to overspend by £19 million in 2026/27.

findings.headline: Slough has not set a balanced 2026/27 budget and has £42.9m of EFS approved in principle
findings.detail: The paper reports that the council cannot balance its 2026/27 budget without additional exceptional financial support. The medium-term plan anticipated a further £22.4 million of EFS in 2027/28.
findings.matters: Reliance on government EFS to balance the budget is a central credit point for lenders, and the scale of the requirement is one a peer council would want to benchmark.
findings.figures: £42.9 million EFS approved in principle for 2026/27; £22.4 million anticipated EFS in 2027/28
findings.quote: The Council has been unable to set a balanced budget for 2026/27 without having additional EFS of £42.9 million approved in principle.

findings.headline: Slough's 2025/26 overspend was £13.2m after £15.7m of EFS, down from a forecast £20.7m
findings.detail: The auditor records that the year-end overspend was reduced from the forecast level through measures introduced during 2025/26, including freezing non-essential recruitment and reducing agency and interim staff. The overspend was predominantly in temporary accommodation and housing benefit subsidy loss.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council facing the same temporary accommodation pressures can compare the in-year containment measures with their own forecast-to-outturn movement.
findings.figures: £13.2 million overspend; £20.7 million forecast overspend; £15.7 million of EFS applied; £13.8 million temporary accommodation and housing benefit subsidy loss
findings.quote: The Council was successful in that a forecast overspend of £20.7 million was contained to an overspend of £13.2 million by year end.

findings.headline: Delays in filing James Elliman Homes accounts have delayed appointments to its board, while options for the entity and its stock are being reviewed.
findings.detail: The paper says the shareholder panel meets monthly and reviews directors' performance on boards. It reports that Cabinet received an options appraisal for James Elliman Homes and an exit strategy for GRE5 in the last year.
findings.matters: Delayed group accounts are a group-exposure point that finance directors at councils with housing companies will check against their own consolidation timetable.
findings.quote: Delays in filing JEH accounts has delayed progress on apoointing to the board, however work continues on reviewing options for the entity and its stock.

findings.headline: The February 2026 capital programme includes £6.32m across 2026/27 to 2030/31 for operational buildings and £5.08m for investment property maintenance.
findings.detail: The paper says the approved capital programme funds works on operational buildings following condition surveys, and maintenance of investment properties to preserve or maximise investment income. The asset management plan identifies incomplete and inconsistent asset data.
findings.matters: Asset-condition funding and incomplete asset data bear on the valuation and disposal assumptions that lenders and finance directors at other councils rely on.
findings.figures: £6.32m across 2026/27 to 2030/31 for operational buildings; £5.08m for investment property maintenance
findings.quote: In February 2026 the Council approved a capital programme including £6.32m of funding across 2026/27 to 2030/31

findings.headline: The paper reports slippage in delivery of individual capital projects, and proposals to spend capital are not always supported by detailed business cases.
findings.detail: The paper says the Capital Board terms of reference have been reviewed. It says delivery slippage on individual projects continues, and that capital spending proposals are not always supported by detailed business cases.
findings.matters: Slippage and capital proposals without business cases are the delivery risks a finance director at another council can check against its own capital programme.
findings.quote: the continued to be slippage in delivery of individual projects.

findings.headline: The Council reports that some longer-standing site disposals have completed and that auctions are achieving good results.
findings.detail: The paper cites completed site disposals and good auction results as evidence of a measured approach to disposal proposals. It sets this against the concern about capital receipts in the MTFS.
findings.matters: Completed disposals and auction results are the delivery evidence a finance director at another council can use when testing its own receipts forecast.
findings.quote: Some longer standing site disposals have recently completed and the Council is achieving good results from auctions.

findings.headline: The paper says there remain concerns about whether MTFS assumptions on capital receipts will be delivered, and that this needs to be kept under review.
findings.detail: The paper says the asset disposal programme has been informed by officer boards evaluating business cases. It says some longer-standing site disposals have completed and auctions are achieving good results.
findings.matters: Capital receipts assumed in the MTFS are the funding line that a finance director at another council will check against its own disposal programme.
findings.quote: There remain concerns as to whether the assumptions in the MTFS on capital receipts will be delivery and this needs to be kept under review

findings.headline: There is still reliance on interim support in key finance roles, including capital finance and dedicated schools grant, though the paper notes more stability than in previous years.
findings.detail: The paper says the director level below the Executive Director is now permanent. It says the new chief executive is considering changes to the chief officer structure to allow longer-term or permanent recruitment in the interim-reliant roles.
findings.matters: Interim reliance in capital finance and DSG is a capacity point that finance directors at other councils face in the same roles.
findings.quote: There remains reliance on interim support in key roles including capital finance and dedicated schools grant, although there has been more stability than in previous years and individuals are suitably experienced.

findings.headline: Internal audit's self-assessment against GIAS shows 37% conformity, 52% partial conformity and 11% non-conformity.
findings.detail: The paper says the Council continues to rely on an interim head of internal audit via CIPFA and additional interim resources. It says the Council has failed to recruit permanently to vacant roles, and an options appraisal of alternative delivery models will go to committee in November.
findings.matters: Internal audit conformity and interim reliance are checks that finance directors at other councils can compare against their own GIAS self-assessments.
findings.figures: 37% conformity; 52% partial conformity; 11% non-conformity
findings.quote: this confirmed 37% conformity, 52% partial conformity and 11% non-conformity with the GIAS standards.

findings.headline: A review against the CIPFA Financial Management Code finds 50% of actions at substantial compliance, 35% at reasonable and 15% at partial or minimal.
findings.detail: The July 2026 report to the committee gives the compliance split. The paper says two areas of minimal assurance, value for money and financial management supporting financial sustainability, remain a focus of the transformation plans.
findings.matters: A finance director can benchmark their own Financial Management Code self-assessment against this split.
findings.figures: 50% substantial compliance; 35% reasonable compliance; 15% partial or minimal compliance
findings.quote: This confirms 50% of actions showing substantial compliance and 35% reasonable compliance, with 15% showing partial or minimal compliance.

findings.headline: Slough produced its draft 2025-26 statement of accounts on time for public inspection and audit.
findings.detail: The paper reports that the draft statement of accounts was produced on time. It notes that the external auditors reported to the committee in July 2026 on the plan to regain assurance.
findings.matters: Meeting the statutory draft accounts deadline after recent audit problems is a point of comparison for finance teams at other councils.
findings.quote: The Council produced its draft statement of accounts 2025-26 on time for public inspection and auditing.

findings.headline: External auditors have assessed Slough as category D, meaning they do not consider it capable of an ISA-compliant approach by 2027/28, and have indicated an intention to use statutory intervention powers.
findings.detail: The paper reports the auditors' category D assessment, citing major systemic problems. It says this year's audit has identified large sample sizes and that it is too early to tell whether weaknesses remain.
findings.matters: A category D assessment and a stated intention to use statutory powers are the audit outcome most likely to affect lenders and peer finance teams.
findings.figures: category D; ISA-compliant approach by 2027/28
findings.quote: The external auditors have assessed the Council as category D, meaning it is not deemed capable of an ISA-compliant approach by 2027/28 due to major systemic problems.

findings.headline: The Council projects a growing dedicated schools grant deficit before any high needs stability grant from 2026/27.
findings.detail: The paper says the Council projects a growing DSG deficit before the high needs stability grant, and that this is reflected in the MTFS. It also says the DfE did not accept the Local Area Reform Plan and an amended plan must be submitted.
findings.matters: A growing DSG deficit with no funded solution is a balance-sheet question that finance directors at councils with high-needs pressures will track.
findings.quote: At present the Council is projecting a growing dedicated schools grant deficit prior to any high needs stability grant from 2026/27

findings.headline: The paper attributes the main overspend to cost pressure in children's social care and says overspends and mitigations are being identified earlier.
findings.detail: The paper describes weekly expenditure control panel reviews by the s.151 officer and chief executive. It says some evidence shows overspends and mitigations are being identified earlier than before.
findings.matters: Early identification of overspends is a monitoring change that a finance director at another council can test against its own forecasting cycle.
findings.quote: The main reason for the overspend relates to cost pressure in children's social care, indicating a greater grip on budgets in other parts of the Council.

findings.headline: The paper reports a significant in-year overspend and a risk that some savings proposals will not be fully implemented in the year.
findings.detail: The Council relies on expenditure control panel processes to control spending. The paper says there is a significant risk of needing to use reserves in-year, which would be contrary to the medium-term reserves strategy.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare an in-year overspend and savings slippage against its own monitoring position.
findings.quote: The Council has a significant in-year overspend and risks that some savings proposals will be be fully implemented in year.

findings.headline: Slough will present an update on the MTFS, not a full draft budget, to the November Cabinet, and still has to prepare a balanced budget for February Cabinet.
findings.detail: The paper says the planned November draft budget was replaced by an MTFS update because of in-year pressures and concerns about the deliverability of savings. It states that further work is required before a balanced budget can go to February Cabinet.
findings.matters: A council that cannot yet present a draft budget in November leaves less time to close a gap before the statutory February setting.
findings.quote: Whilst there was an intention to have a draft budget presented to Cabinet in November, in-year financial pressures and concerns about deliverability of savings proposals, has meant that officers will present an update on the MTFS position but not a full draft budget.

findings.headline: The 2025/26 outturn required a £13.2m drawdown on reserves, with 25.8% of savings proposals not fully delivered in that year.
findings.detail: The Council approved a new reserves strategy in March 2026, but the 2025/26 outturn report required drawing on reserves. The paper links this partly to savings non-delivery and says the Council has commissioned a transformation partner.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the size of the reserves drawdown and the savings shortfall against its own outturn.
findings.figures: £13.2m drawdown on reserves; 25.8% of savings proposals not fully delivered in 2025/26
findings.quote: the 2025/26 outturn report confirmed the need to drawdown on reserves to the sum of £13.2m, partly due to 25.8% of savings proposals not being fully delivered in that year

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: The Head of Internal Audit's delivery model is to be reviewed because of challenges in permanent recruitment
findings.detail: The paper says the Head of Internal Audit's annual opinion and plan are reported to the committee at least quarterly, and that a new Audit Board is in place. It also states that the delivery model needs review because permanent recruitment has been difficult.
findings.matters: Recruitment difficulty in internal audit leadership is a pressure that other councils' audit functions also report.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: review of delivery model required due to challenges in permanent recruitment.

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: A new Chief Executive is to consider timetabling the corporate plan refresh around the May 2027 elections
findings.detail: The paper lists a new Chief Executive as the officer responsible for several next steps, including whether performance reporting should move to quarterly for CLT. The corporate plan refresh is to be timed with the May 2027 elections in view.
findings.matters: A change of chief executive combined with a corporate plan refresh before elections affects the council's strategic planning timetable.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: New CE to consider timetabling for refresh of corporate plan taking account of May 2027 elections.

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: Risk of fraud linked to internal controls is recorded as a corporate risk
findings.detail: The paper says that fraud risk arising from internal control weaknesses is recorded as a corporate risk. Counter fraud reporting to CLT is mainly on activity rather than assurance, and the next step is annual assurance on fraud risks and a maturity assessment.
findings.matters: Fraud risk recorded at corporate level, with planned annual assurance, is a point of comparison for other councils' counter-fraud arrangements.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: Risk of fraud in response to poor internal controls raised as a corporate risk.

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: Performance against the AGS action plan is aligned to work in the Finance Improvement Plan
findings.detail: The paper says the Corporate Governance Working Group is responsible for performance against the Annual Governance Statement action plan, and that this is aligned to the Finance Improvement Plan. Quarterly updates on the AGS action plan go to the Audit and Corporate Governance Committee.
findings.matters: A finance improvement plan linked to the governance action plan is a reference point for other councils with similar plans.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: aligned to work in Finance Improvement Plan.

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: The shareholder panel for council companies is described as operating well and leading to officer recommendations on companies
findings.detail: The paper says the shareholder panel is operating well and produces officer recommendations on companies. It also notes that partnership reporting is still limited and that a strategic partnership audit has been commissioned but not yet concluded.
findings.matters: Council-owned companies are a common source of contingent liabilities, and a lender would want to know whether oversight of them is working.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: The shareholder panel is operating well and leading to officer recommendations on companies.

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: Internal audit of whistleblowing shows "reasonable assurance"
findings.detail: The paper reports that the whistleblowing policy has been reviewed and is to be approved by Full Council in September. The Monitoring Officer's assurance tools include an internal audit of whistleblowing that is described as in progress in one section and as completed in another.
findings.matters: A reasonable-assurance result on an ethics control gives a peer council a benchmark for its own whistleblowing audits.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: Internal audit for whistleblowing shows reasonable assurance

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: The Procurement Review Board still sees rolled over contracts, direct awards or extensions, and the contracts register is not up to date
findings.detail: The paper states that the Procurement Review Board is in existence but that examples of rolled over contracts, direct awards and extensions remain, attributed to lack of planning and an out-of-date contracts register. Next steps include changes to the board's focus and earlier cabinet approval for procurements.
findings.matters: Direct awards and rolled over contracts can signal weak procurement control, and peer councils face the same pressures.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: contracts, direct awards or extensions due to lack of planning and contracts register not being up to date

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: The Section 151 Officer and Chief Executive are to consider whether budget reporting to CLT captures overspend or slippage risks on the capital programme
findings.detail: The paper says the Capital Board's terms of reference have been reviewed. It also records that the next step is to decide whether current CLT budget reporting captures capital overspend or slippage risks and informs discussion of mitigations.
findings.matters: Capital overspend and slippage reporting is a common gap for councils, and a lender would want to see whether the risk is being escalated to senior officers.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: is capturing risks of overspend or slippage on capital programme

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: Savings tracker delivery is presented in different ways by different finance teams
findings.detail: The paper records that savings tracking is reported to CLT monthly and to Cabinet quarterly, but the format differs between finance teams. No savings figures are given in this document.
findings.matters: Inconsistent savings tracking makes it harder for members and officers to judge whether budget savings are being delivered.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: Savings tracker delivery presented in different ways by different finance teams.

findings.paper_title: AGS Appendix 2 - LGA Improvement and Assurance Framework Assessment
findings.headline: Executive Director expected to attend the Audit and Corporate Governance Committee to respond to concerns about "lack of attention to internal audits and delay in implementation"
findings.detail: The paper states that the Executive Director will be invited to the committee to respond to these concerns. It also says that a new Audit Board has been set up and has met once, and that DLTs should ensure internal audit data is a feature of their meetings.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, would want to know that internal audit actions are running late at a council with a live finance improvement plan.
findings.figures: none stated
findings.quote: Executive Director expected to attend Audit and Corporate Governance Committee on invite to respond to concerns about lack of attention to internal audits and delay in implementation.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement - Quarter 2 Update Report
findings.headline: The paper reports significant progress on updating policies and procedures, including reporting lines for declarations of interests and other approvals.
findings.detail: The workforce theme has one red and two amber ratings. The paper says progress has been made on updating policies and procedures, and that further work is required on leadership capacity and recruitment.
findings.matters: Improvement in declarations of interest and approval reporting lines is a control improvement that peer councils and lenders assessing governance quality will look for.
findings.figures: Workforce theme RAG ratings: 1 red, 2 amber (counts)
findings.quote: Significant progress has been made on updating policies and procedures, including

findings.headline: The Council says there remain concerns about delivery of capital projects on time.
findings.detail: The procurement and contract management theme is rated one red and two amber. Alongside the statement on capital delivery, the paper notes that early engagement with procurement and legal on commissioning proposals still needs improvement.
findings.matters: Capital schemes running late are a recognised pressure on council borrowing and cash flow, and peers will compare how councils report delivery risk.
findings.figures: Procurement and contract management theme RAG ratings: 1 red, 2 amber (counts)
findings.quote: there remain concerns around delivery of capital projects on time.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement - Quarter 2 Update Report
findings.headline: Slough Children First received an Ofsted inspection highlighting significant concerns, and the paper says a new business plan is not expected until January 2027.
findings.detail: The board of Slough Children First is reviewing structures for appropriate governance. The Council has commissioned external support to review performance and financial efficiency before deciding in-year and future-year funding.
findings.matters: A children's trust under an Ofsted concern, with its business plan and funding decisions deferred, is a service and cost risk that other councils running similar arrangements will track.
findings.quote: A new business plan is not expected until January 2027.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement - Quarter 2 Update Report
findings.headline: The DfE did not approve the Council's Local Area Reform Plan, placing risk around funding to mitigate the dedicated schools grant deficit
findings.detail: The children's services theme has two red and one amber rating. The paper says the DfE has not approved the Local Area Reform Plan, creating risk around funding to mitigate the dedicated schools grant deficit.
findings.matters: A DSG deficit whose mitigation plan has not been approved by the DfE leaves the funding route uncertain, which is a central question for councils with a DSG deficit.

findings.paper_title: Slough Council Audit progress report and sector update September 2026
findings.headline: Debtor and creditor balances lack clean transaction data, driving abnormally large sample sizes and delaying audit completion.
findings.detail: The council's financial system derives debtor and creditor lists by rolling forward prior balances and adjusting for in-year transactions. This method makes it impossible to identify which items are actual year-end balances, since tested items may have already been paid or received. The council has attempted cleansing but substantial duplicate and contradictory entries remain. The auditors recommend full transaction listing cleansing before next year's audit.
findings.matters: Unreliable financial data in the accounts production process indicates control weaknesses that increase audit risk and governance concerns for lenders assessing financial systems integrity.
findings.figures: 948 total sample items selected; 549 (58%) remain outstanding as at report date. Creditors testing: 31 outstanding; Payments made: 23 outstanding.
findings.quote: Break downs provided, from the financial system, to support these balances were derived from a balance bought forward adjusted for in year receipts and payments. This makes selecting samples for testing difficult as items tested could have been paid or received and are therefore no longer year end balances.

Commissioners are content with the recommendations but note full mitigation proposals will be reported at Q2.
findings.matters: A lender would view commissioner intervention and the explicit warning about governance as a red flag indicating the council is unable to manage its finances independently and requires external control; the emphasis on political-officer alignment suggests confidence is fragile.

findings.headline: Council Tax collection is 0.15% behind target at 35.95%, with residents continuing to struggle with cost-of-living increases and most Berkshire councils falling behind their prior-year position.

The full-year collection target of 93.5% is expected to be achieved due to additional recovery processes being implemented in 2026/27, but the in-year position indicates underlying resident financial distress.
findings.matters: A lender would view council tax collection performance as an early warning indicator of resident financial stress and the council's ability to sustain income in future years; widespread collections weakness across the region suggests a structural problem rather than a council-specific issue.

findings.matters: A lender would be aware that rising gilt yields increase the cost of council borrowing; this demonstrates the council's exposure to external interest rate movements and the difficulty of forecasting interest costs in a rising rate environment.

findings.paper_title: Housing Benefit War Pension Disregard Policy Report
